text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
The government is to announce a package of measures to cut public expenditure by at least 1 billion reais.
-- WHY THE CENTRAL BANK WANTS $1 BILLION

An unnamed Central Bank source said the government was looking at ways to use an increase in foreign reserves, generated by the emmission of a $1 billion "global" bonus, to reduce the treasury's internal debt.

The Finance Ministry has barred airlines from increasing their fares before June 1997 to make up for the ICMS tax, levied on the sale and circulation of goods and services, they will have to pay as of November 1.
-- ONE THIRD OF VOTERS DON'T UNDERSTAND RE-ELECTION
A survey has found one third of Brazilian voters does not understand the term re-election properly, but 51 percent approve of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's re-election.
-- MINAS GERAIS GETS 2.5 BLN REAIS TO SELL BANKS
The federal government will give 2.5 billion reais to the state of Minas Gerais for the privatization of state banks Credireal and Bemge.
-- GOVT WANTS TO END ISS TAX ON EXPORTS
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the government wanted to end the ISS service tax on exports and investments in the production of machines.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
